records.originalText: If you pump air into a tire, it expands.

records.originalText: She got a job as a typist.

records.originalText: The dynamite went off with a bang.

records.originalText: As a rule, I go to school before eight o'clock.

records.originalText: Most students come to school on foot.

records.originalText: I am sorry I have imposed so much on you.
records.finalText: I am sorry I have imposed so much on you.

records.originalText: She failed the examination and I was greatly disappointed.
records.finalText: She failed the examination and I was greatly disappointed.

records.originalText: There's little chance of keeping slim, unless you stick to a diet.
records.finalText: There's little chance of keeping slim, unless you stick to a diet.

records.finalText: She's lost a lot of weight since she went on a diet.

records.originalText: The diamond was set in a gold ring.
records.finalText: The diamond was set in a gold ring.

records.originalText: Go out of the terminal and turn right.
records.finalText: Go out of the terminal and turn right.

records.originalText: The Soviet troops started to withdraw from Afghanistan.
records.finalText: The Soviet troops started to withdraw from Afghanistan.

records.finalText: It is fortunate that you have such parents.

records.originalText: Don't beat your head against a stone wall.
records.finalText: Don't beat your head against a stone wall.

records.originalText: It is stupid of him to behave like that.
records.finalText: It is stupid of him to behave like that.

records.finalText: Don't make such careless mistakes.

records.finalText: It is no use arguing with such a foolish man.

records.originalText: It is stupid of you to make such a mistake.

records.originalText: Such an old fan would be next to useless.

records.originalText: Don't put it that way.

records.originalText: Don't run down the stairs so noisily.

records.finalText: Don't shout like that. I can hear you perfectly.

records.finalText: We'll get along without that much money somehow.

records.finalText: It was foolish of him to waste his money on such trifles.

records.originalText: You ought not to say such a thing.

records.finalText: What is the good of doing it?

records.originalText: How did you hit upon such an idea?

records.originalText: It is no use worrying about it.

records.rationale: By the Queen herself correctly expresses an emphatic passive agent in a particular gift account.

records.originalText: That will benefit the community.
records.finalText: That will benefit the community.
records.rationale: The proposed community benefit has no project or action referent, leaving an unsupported bare prediction.

records.originalText: It is just an act.
records.finalText: It is just an act.
records.rationale: Just an act is a conventional figurative evaluation that behavior is performed rather than sincere.

records.originalText: Far from being a failure, it was a great success.
records.finalText: Far from being a failure, it was a great success.
records.rationale: Far from being a failure correctly contrasts two explicit outcome evaluations in a complete speaker assessment.

records.originalText: That runs against my principles.
records.finalText: That goes against my principles.
records.rationale: Use goes against for the natural principles collocation while preserving the speaker's objection.

records.originalText: That is my own affair.
records.finalText: That is my own affair.
records.rationale: Same personal-privacy assertion as the published none-of-your-beeswax idiom, without a distinct event.

records.originalText: It's a whole new ball game for me.
records.finalText: It's a whole new ball game for me.
records.rationale: A whole new ball game is an established idiom for a substantially changed personal situation.

records.originalText: It is of little consequence to me.
records.finalText: It is of little consequence to me.
records.rationale: Of little consequence to me is a valid formal expression of limited personal importance.

records.originalText: It is nothing to me.
records.finalText: It is nothing to me.
records.rationale: Repeats 42385's statement of personal lack of importance using the simpler nothing-to-me expression.

records.originalText: It was a nervous moment for me.
records.finalText: It was a nervous moment for me.
records.rationale: A nervous moment for me is a natural specific past emotional-event description.

records.originalText: That has nothing to do with me.
records.finalText: That has nothing to do with me.
records.rationale: Nothing to do with me is a conventional complete denial of involvement, distinct from indifference.

records.originalText: Does that mean you want to break up?
records.finalText: Does that mean you want to break up?
records.rationale: The question explicitly identifies ending a relationship as the proposed interpretation.

records.originalText: It is like the air we breathe.
records.finalText: It is like the air we breathe.
records.rationale: The comparison subject is absent, leaving like-the-air-we-breathe an unexplained metaphor.

records.originalText: I am to blame for it.
records.finalText: I am to blame for it.
records.rationale: To blame for it is a conventional complete acknowledgment of personal responsibility.

records.originalText: It was my first night among strangers.
records.finalText: It was my first night among strangers.
records.rationale: First night among strangers supplies an independent personal setting and a clear past description.

records.originalText: That's the same story as I heard when I was a child.
records.finalText: That's the same story as I heard when I was a child.
records.rationale: The relative clause explicitly locates the same story in the speaker's childhood experience.

records.originalText: It is a childish act.
records.finalText: It is a childish act.
records.rationale: The childish-act judgment identifies no act and adds only a context-dependent negative label.

records.originalText: It is only too true.
records.finalText: It is only too true.
records.rationale: Only too true is a bare agreement reaction with no proposition to evaluate.

records.originalText: Isn't that the most humane punishment for criminals?
records.finalText: Isn't that the most humane punishment for criminals?
records.rationale: The unnamed punishment and leading humane-superlative question require legal and ethical context absent from the source.

records.originalText: That's a matter of prime importance.
records.finalText: That's a matter of prime importance.
records.rationale: A matter of prime importance is a conventional complete priority assessment in formal direct speech.

records.originalText: That is not the point in question.
records.finalText: That is not the point in question.
records.rationale: Repeats the existing question-is-not-relevant-to-the-subject relevance correction with another point-in-question expression.

records.originalText: It may occur at any moment.
records.finalText: It may occur at any moment.
records.rationale: The event that may occur is unidentified, making the timing warning independently uninterpretable.

records.originalText: It is the in thing to do.
records.finalText: It is the in thing to do.
records.rationale: The activity and fashion context are absent from the changing in-thing claim.

records.originalText: It was nothing but the shadow of a tall tree.
records.finalText: It was nothing but the shadow of a tall tree.
records.rationale: Nothing but the shadow of a tall tree is a clear concrete identification of an initially uncertain sight.

records.originalText: That is going too far.
records.finalText: That is going too far.
records.rationale: Going too far is a conventional complete objection that an action exceeds an acceptable limit.

records.originalText: It is like letting a tiger run loose.
records.finalText: It is like letting a tiger run loose.
records.rationale: The unnamed act and loose-tiger simile provide no independent context for the proposed danger comparison.

records.originalText: It is by no means an easy job.
records.finalText: It is by no means an easy job.
records.rationale: By no means correctly strengthens the evaluation of the explicitly stated job's difficulty.

records.originalText: It is merely a matter of form.
records.finalText: It is merely a matter of form.
records.rationale: A matter of form is a conventional complete expression for a required formality.

records.originalText: It was a chance meeting.
records.finalText: It was a chance meeting.
records.rationale: A chance meeting is a natural, independently interpretable specific-event description.

records.originalText: It can't be measured in terms of money.
records.finalText: It can't be measured in terms of money.
records.rationale: Measured in terms of money is a natural figurative value expression in a complete modal passive.

records.originalText: It was the greatest earthquake on record.
records.finalText: It was the greatest earthquake on record.
records.rationale: The record earthquake lacks an identified event, location, measurement and historical cutoff.

records.originalText: Is it sweet or sour?
records.finalText: Is it sweet or sour?
records.rationale: The sweet-or-sour question is a natural complete food-taste enquiry in direct speech.

records.originalText: I'll look forward to it.
records.finalText: I'll look forward to it.
records.rationale: Repeats the positive anticipation already published in the get-together-and-looking-forward-to-it utterance.

records.originalText: Can I take your word for it?
records.finalText: Can I take your word for it?
records.rationale: Repeats the existing take-my-word-for-it trust-assurance idiom as a question with no new situation.

records.originalText: It has an important influence upon our lives.
records.finalText: It has an important influence upon our lives.
records.rationale: The thing influencing our lives and the affected population are both unspecified.

records.originalText: It was a blow to us.
records.finalText: It was a blow to us.
records.rationale: A blow to us is a natural metaphor for a particular group's setback.

records.originalText: It will do harm to us.
records.finalText: It will do harm to us.
records.rationale: The harmful action or object is unidentified, so the prediction cannot stand independently.

records.originalText: It's a problem we do not have any answer for.
records.finalText: It's a problem we do not have any answer for.
records.rationale: The problem-with-no-answer relative clause is a complete statement of unresolved difficulty.

records.originalText: It was one of the great discoveries in science.
records.finalText: It was one of the great discoveries in science.
records.rationale: The unnamed discovery and unqualified great-discovery ranking lack necessary scientific context.

records.originalText: It is something like a ball.
records.finalText: It is something like a ball.
records.rationale: Something like a ball is a natural approximate-shape description with a concrete comparison object.

records.originalText: That may easily have been a mistake.
records.finalText: That may easily have been a mistake.
records.rationale: May have been correctly expresses tentative retrospective assessment of a possible mistake.

records.originalText: How did it all come about?
records.finalText: How did it all come about?
records.rationale: The event referenced by it all is absent and the come-about question repeats existing event-origin enquiries.

records.originalText: It leaves nothing much to be desired.
records.finalText: It leaves nothing much to be desired.
records.rationale: Leaves nothing much to be desired is a conventional positive evaluation using the desired idiom correctly.

records.originalText: That is not quite what I wanted.
records.finalText: That is not quite what I wanted.
records.rationale: Not quite what I wanted naturally expresses a specific mismatch with the speaker's preference.

records.originalText: I'm not sure about that. It depends.
records.finalText: I'm not sure about that. It depends.
records.rationale: The uncertainty statement and it depends are conventional complete qualified responses in direct speech.

records.originalText: It was hard as rock.
records.finalText: It was hard as rock.
records.rationale: Hard as rock is a natural conventional simile for a material's hardness.

records.originalText: It sounds as if he were to blame for the disaster.
records.finalText: It sounds as if he were to blame for the disaster.
records.rationale: As if plus were to blame grammatically frames a tentative causal attribution about a specified disaster.

records.originalText: That is quite another matter.
records.finalText: That is quite another matter.
records.rationale: Quite another matter is a conventional complete expression distinguishing a separate issue.

records.originalText: It is still in the testing stage.
records.finalText: It is still in the testing stage.
records.rationale: In the testing stage is a natural stage-of-development collocation within a complete status statement.

records.originalText: Let's reserve that for another occasion.
records.finalText: Let's reserve that for another occasion.
records.rationale: Reserve that for another occasion is a natural complete suggestion to postpone a topic or activity.

records.originalText: It was just something I read in a newspaper.
records.finalText: It was just something I read in a newspaper.
records.rationale: The newspaper relative clause identifies the speaker's information channel without asserting its reliability.

records.originalText: It happened just like this.
records.finalText: It happened just like this.
records.rationale: Just like this points to a missing demonstration, leaving the event description wholly absent.

records.originalText: It's only a small house but it meets my needs perfectly.
records.finalText: It's only a small house but it meets my needs perfectly.
records.rationale: The small-house description explicitly balances size with adequacy for the speaker's needs.

records.originalText: It is of little value.
records.finalText: It is of little value.
records.rationale: The object with little value is unidentified and repeats the batch's context-only value assessments.

records.originalText: That's nonsense. Nobody but a fool would believe it.
records.finalText: That's nonsense. Nobody but a fool would believe it.
records.rationale: The bare nonsense-and-fool insult supplies neither a proposition nor suitable independent learning context.

records.originalText: That is a trivial problem.
records.finalText: That is a trivial problem.
records.rationale: A trivial problem is a grammatical complete subjective assessment of an issue's limited importance.

records.originalText: You find it in any dictionary.
records.finalText: You find it in any dictionary.
records.rationale: The dictionary item is unidentified and any dictionary is an unsupported universal availability claim.

records.originalText: It grew larger and larger.
records.finalText: It grew larger and larger.
records.rationale: Larger and larger naturally expresses progressive physical growth in a complete past description.

records.originalText: It moved closer and closer.
records.finalText: It moved closer and closer.
records.rationale: Closer and closer naturally expresses progressive approach, a distinct spatial event from size growth.

records.originalText: It is so dreadful that I don't want to think of it.
records.finalText: It is so dreadful that I don't want to think of it.
records.rationale: So dreadful that correctly connects a subjective assessment with the speaker's reluctance to think about it.

records.originalText: It was such a shock.
records.finalText: It was such a shock.
records.rationale: Such a shock is a conventional complete emotional-event exclamation in past declarative form.

records.originalText: It's a hard, dirty job.
records.finalText: It's a hard, dirty job.
records.rationale: Hard dirty job supplies an independently understandable description of a specific type of work.
